HOA MEMBER DISCIPLINE AND FINES — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Maple Grove Homeowners Association · September 1, 2026

HOA MEMBER DISCIPLINE AND FINES — INTRODUCTION AND SCOPE
This information sheet describes, in general terms, the procedural due-process requirements that the Davis-Stirling Common Interest Development Act imposes on a California common interest development association before its board may impose a monetary penalty (fine), impose a monetary charge to reimburse the association for common-area damage, or otherwise discipline a member for an alleged violation of the governing documents, in connection with Maple Grove Homeowners Association. The relevant statutory provisions are Civil Code §§ 5850, 5855, and 5865, part of Article 1 ("Discipline and Cost Reimbursement") of Chapter 10 ("Dispute Resolution and Enforcement") of the Act, together with the related internal dispute resolution provisions of Civil Code § 5910 in Article 2 of that same chapter. This topic — the pre-fine notice-and-hearing procedure and the board's internal disciplinary process — is distinct from a seller's document-disclosure obligations to a buyer under the Act's disclosure article (addressed in this corpus's HOA/CC&R Disclosure document), from an association's lien and nonjudicial foreclosure remedy for delinquent assessments (addressed in this corpus's HOA Assessment Lien and Foreclosure — Information Sheet), from the secret-ballot procedures that govern certain membership votes (addressed in this corpus's HOA Board Election Procedures — Information Sheet), and from the open-meeting notice and agenda requirements for board meetings generally (addressed in this corpus's Common Interest Development Open Meeting Act — Information Sheet). This sheet is informational only. It does not itself notice, conduct, or decide any disciplinary hearing; it does not impose, waive, reduce, or collect any fine or monetary charge; it does not invoke or conduct any internal dispute resolution procedure; and it does not determine whether any actual notice, hearing, decision, or fine relating to Maple Grove Homeowners Association has complied — or failed to comply — with the statutory requirements it describes.

MONETARY PENALTY SCHEDULE AND STATUTORY CAP
Before an association may impose a monetary penalty on a member for a violation of the governing documents, California law requires the board to have adopted and distributed a schedule of the penalties that may be assessed. Civil Code § 5850(a) provides that if an association adopts a policy imposing a monetary penalty for a violation of the governing documents, "the board shall adopt and distribute to each member, in the annual policy statement prepared pursuant to Section 5310, a schedule of the monetary penalties that may be assessed for those violations, which shall be in accordance with authorization for member discipline contained in the governing documents. Monetary penalties shall be reasonable." A new or revised penalty may instead be distributed in an individual supplement under Section 4040. Section 5850(c) caps most penalties: "A monetary penalty for a violation of the governing documents shall not exceed the lesser of the following: (1) The monetary penalty stated in the schedule of monetary penalties or supplement that is in effect at the time of the violation. (2) One hundred dollars ($100) per violation." Section 5850(d) allows a higher penalty only for a violation with adverse health or safety consequences, and only after a specific written finding: "Notwithstanding subdivision (c), the board may impose a penalty stated in the schedule of monetary penalties or supplement that is in effect at the time of the violation that is greater than one hundred dollars ($100) per violation, if the violation may result in an adverse health or safety impact on the common area or another association member’s property. (2) Before imposing a penalty on a violation pursuant to this subdivision, the board shall make a written finding specifying the adverse health or safety impact in a board meeting open to the members." Section 5850(e) provides: "A late charge or interest shall not be charged to a member for a monetary penalty." Section 5850(f) provides: "An association shall provide a copy of the most recently distributed schedule of monetary penalties, along with any applicable supplements to that schedule, to any member upon request." These requirements concern Maple Grove Homeowners Association in general terms; this clause does not state what Maple Grove Homeowners Association's own schedule of monetary penalties provides or whether any specific penalty amount complies with it.

REQUIRED NOTICE AND HEARING BEFORE DISCIPLINE
Before a board may consider or impose discipline on a member — or impose a monetary charge to reimburse the association for repairing damage to the common area or facilities caused by a member or the member's guest or tenant — California law requires advance written notice of the meeting at which the matter will be considered. Civil Code § 5855(a) provides that "the board shall notify the member in writing, by either personal delivery or individual delivery pursuant to Section 4040, at least 10 days prior to the meeting." Section 5855(b) specifies the minimum content of that notice and the member's rights at the meeting: "The notification shall contain, at a minimum, the date, time, and place of the meeting, the nature of the alleged violation for which a member may be disciplined or the nature of the damage to the common area and facilities for which a monetary charge may be imposed, and a statement that the member has a right to attend and may address the board at the meeting. The board shall meet in executive session if requested by the member." Section 5855(c) requires that the member be given a chance to cure the violation before discipline may be imposed: "A member shall have the opportunity to cure the violation prior to the meeting. The board shall not impose discipline in either of the following circumstances: (1) The member cures the violation prior to the meeting. (2) If curing the violation would take longer than the time between the notice provided pursuant to subdivision (a) and the meeting, the member provides financial commitment to cure the violation." These notice, attendance, executive-session, and cure-opportunity requirements apply to Maple Grove Homeowners Association in general terms; this clause does not describe the content of any specific notice issued by, or any specific hearing held by, Maple Grove Homeowners Association.

OUTCOME OF THE MEETING AND WRITTEN DECISION
California law specifies what must happen after the board's disciplinary meeting concludes, depending on whether the board and the member reach agreement, and requires written notice of any decision to discipline. Civil Code § 5855(d) addresses disagreement: "If the board and the member are not in agreement after the meeting, a member shall have the opportunity to request internal dispute resolution pursuant to Section 5910." Section 5855(e) addresses agreement: "If the board and the member are in agreement after the meeting, the board shall draft a written resolution. The written resolution, signed by the board and the member of the dispute pursuant to procedures not in conflict with the law or governing documents, binds the association and is judicially enforceable." Section 5855(f) requires written notice of an adverse decision within a fixed period: "If the board imposes discipline on a member or imposes a monetary charge on the member for damage to the common area and facilities, the board shall provide the member with a written notification of the decision, by either personal delivery or individual delivery pursuant to Section 4040, within 14 days following the action." Section 5855(g) ties the validity of the discipline to compliance with all of these requirements: "A disciplinary action or the imposition of a monetary charge for damage to the common area shall not be effective against a member unless the board fulfills the requirements of this section." Separately, Civil Code § 5865 clarifies that none of this is meant to expand or narrow the board's underlying disciplinary authority: "Nothing in Section 5850 or 5855 shall be construed to create, expand, or reduce the authority of the board to impose monetary penalties on a member for a violation of the governing documents." These provisions concern Maple Grove Homeowners Association in general terms; this clause does not state whether the board of Maple Grove Homeowners Association reached agreement with any specific member, issued any specific written resolution or written notification, or met the 14-day deadline in any specific instance.

INTERNAL DISPUTE RESOLUTION — A RELATED BUT SEPARATE PROCEDURE
The Davis-Stirling Act contains a separate procedure, distinct from the disciplinary notice-and-meeting process itself, called internal dispute resolution (IDR). Civil Code § 5855(d) allows a member who disagrees with the board's disciplinary decision to "request internal dispute resolution pursuant to Section 5910," and Civil Code § 5910, in Article 2 of the same chapter, sets the minimum requirements any such association procedure must meet: "A fair, reasonable, and expeditious dispute resolution procedure shall, at a minimum, satisfy all of the following requirements:". Among those requirements, Section 5910(c) and (d) address who must participate: "If the procedure is invoked by a member, the association shall participate in the procedure," while "If the procedure is invoked by the association, the member may elect not to participate in the procedure. If the member participates but the dispute is resolved other than by agreement of the member, the member shall have a right of appeal to the board." Section 5910(f) addresses the parties' ability to explain their positions: "The procedure shall provide a means by which the member and the association may explain their positions. The member and association may be assisted by an attorney or another person in explaining their positions at their own cost." Section 5910(g) provides: "A member of the association shall not be charged a fee to participate in the process." IDR under § 5910 is a post-decision, member-invocable dispute procedure that operates alongside the discipline-specific notice-and-meeting requirements of § 5855; it is not itself the pre-fine hearing described elsewhere in this document. This provision concerns Maple Grove Homeowners Association in general terms; this clause does not state what IDR procedure Maple Grove Homeowners Association has adopted or whether any specific IDR request has been made.

Section 5910(f) addresses the parties' ability to explain their positions: "The procedure shall provide a means by which the member and the association may explain their positions.
